detail: The Governor's own awardee PDF reconciles EXACTLY with the committed file: 81 awardees and $188,201,256.11 against 81 rows and $188,201,256.11. The source numbers 1-82 and skips 66 -- a gap in the Governor's office's numbering, not the parse's. AHCA's own page publishes no roster and points at this release. The release also refers to an EARLIER procurement round for monitoring and support vendors whose recipients are not published anywhere reachable.

CLOSED IN SESSION 22. The two signed Notices of Award on greathealth.georgia.gov/find-funding-opportunities -- the page this re-check read first -- name 21 hospital award actions worth $30,277,580, and ga_great_health_awards.csv now carries all 21 as named rows citing the notice. Joined on DCH's own GREAT application number, not on the hospital name. No aggregate row reading 'names not captured' survives. The dollars were always inside Georgia's $197,148,327 at POOL level, so the state total did not move: what moved is $30,277,580 from pooled to named, taking Georgia's named-hospital figure from $60,000,000 to $90,277,580.

The eligible-projects table is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed archive (67 table rows, 66 projects). DHS's funding-opportunities page -- a child never read -- lists 4 further payment programmes worth about $86,800,000 and names NO recipient for any of them. Eligibility is not receipt (§0.3); there is nothing here to extract.

The governor's release is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed archive, so the 138 grants stand. alabamarhtp.com is still a solicitation site: 10 closed NOFOs, no award file in any format, and the home page states Year 1 application periods are now closed.

CLOSED IN SESSION 22, AND IT WILL RE-OPEN. The rolling notice grew from 161 to 185 award actions and $160,701,975 to $181,871,366 -- 24 new awards ($16,862,504) plus one existing award revised upward ($4,306,887, Southcentral Foundation BP1-IA-308). ak_year1_awardees.csv now carries 185 rows and $181,871,366, and this check compares against THAT rather than against a named evidence file, so it cannot go on reporting a gap it has closed. 0 award action(s) are on the notice and not in the committed file. Alaska's own Year 1 Funding Cycle Update corroborates the total independently at 185 projects and says awards are announced on a rolling weekly basis -- so Alaska needs a SCHEDULE, not an extraction: R/03h --probe is the weekly check.

The awards page and the Catalyst data file are unchanged (the xlsx is byte-identical). The RHTP home page links 12 GovDelivery bulletins and session 17 read ONE of them; the other eleven were read here and none is a roster -- they are webinar invitations, deadline extensions, RFGP addenda and the two December award announcements already archived. Wave 2 is still 21 of OHA's stated 33.

HFS still publishes no recipient-level award list; il.amplifund.com is behind a sign-in. The one recipient-level document is the Hospital Planning Grant Methodology, which names 97 ELIGIBLE hospitals WITH CCNs against a $28,191,393 pool and states its per-hospital figure conditionally ('if all hospitals apply'). §0.3: that is eligibility, not receipt, and nothing was coded from it. The CCN list is worth keeping for open blocker 5.
